chunk_map.heading: The team lead's piece: what agents do here, agreed together

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-8: 'What do the agents do: draft the digest, sort the tickets' - nearest miss; 'the digest'/'the tickets' are illustrative example tasks inside a verbed question list, not referents to an earlier slide; 'The team lead's piece' is named in the header (in-chunk). Harm (unresolvable referent) absent.
L4-8: no pointer at another file or slide by position; grep for 'lecture|module|earlier|last' in body returns none.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-8: no 'the X you did/saw' reference; closest is 'the draft the team decides on' (L4), which is defined in the same sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L6: 'What do the agents do: ...?' - nearest to a demo cue but a question list with verbs, no guess/reveal beat.
L4: chunk carries a self-carrying claim (team decision, working agreement) plus three question families and a quote; not an orphan.
L1 header 'what agents do here, agreed together' vs L4-8: body states a working agreement the team decides on; header is literally true.

L4: 'a team decision, not one enthusiast's' - closest to a tic; a single 'X, not Y' contrast, not 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'; no triples, superlatives, number+retraction, abstraction stacks or empty verb triplets (L6 'draft the digest, sort the tickets, build rough prototypes' - three concrete legs).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-8: body has no repo/authorial dialect; 'the team lead's piece' is the training's role-piece naming used plainly. Closest: 'working agreement' (ordinary team vocabulary).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep '\*\*' on body L1-9 -> 0 bold; within budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single ## chunk with slide id; has_slide_includes false; no phase-less prose section concerns for a slide file included by its lecture.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/slides/working-agreements-with-agents.md -> 'OK - 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.'; header carries no hand number.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file ... -> 'OK - 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file ... -> oversized: 0 (1 slide, limits 210 words / 6 bullets).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 header is a label-plus-claim ('what agents do here, agreed together'); orientation/catalogue-style header for a role piece, not a law slide, so the claim requirement does not bind.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L8 Marquet quote: closest to a kicker, but it adds a new object (who decides: push authority to people with the information) and is attributed and backed (marquet-push-authority-2015); not a restatement of the header; L4 first sentence not restated later.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: no header rename evidenced: maintainer STATUS says rebuilt as new slide 2026-10-07; body is a single fresh set answering the current header.

notes: Single-chunk slide file; the slide is the ## itself (no separate H1 lede). Rule 13 N/A: no links. Rule 1 judged on the file alone; 'the team lead's piece' is a header-named term. Marquet quote fidelity (Wayback-only) is a research-claims matter, not slides.
